metadata.name: Workflow Management Flow
metadata.description: Creates or edits one complete Moira workflow through source reconciliation, evidence-aware requirements and design, official CLI mutation, structural projection, and independent review. For meaningful user-visible stages it authors optional static progress shared by the always-visible UI and PNG delivery, including truthful active-only role or unit detail on mapped waiting nodes while inactive milestones remain stable. It preserves semantic evidence boundaries, cause-aware repair/replan, autonomous or interactive approvals, explicit publication authority and repository identity. Use it to create or change workflow definitions; it does not execute the downstream task.
metadata.author: mcp-moira-team

nodes.directive:
Determine whether the user wants to create a workflow or edit an existing one, and how this run treats the user. Reuse an explicit decision without asking again.

For edit, resolve the workflow identity (public `owner/slug`, internal ID, or another exact identity), whether server access is permitted, and any explicit local path hint. Ask only for a material fact that is not already present and cannot be discovered. Do not search, download, create a workspace, or analyze the workflow here.

Resolve the one canonical `workspace_path` without creating it. Use a filesystem-safe short label derived from the requested workflow name or identity for create, and from the resolved slug or ID for edit. Preserve this exact convention: `./moira-ws/workflow-management-flow-{name-or-id}-{action}-{YYYYMMDD}-{HHMM}`. The action segment is `create` or `edit`; the timestamp is the current local date and time. Do not create an alias or a second workspace path.

Resolve `operating_mode` in this same turn:

- return the mode the user already stated, without asking again;
- infer it when it is unambiguous — for example an explicit instruction to work without interruptions, or running as a child of a process that is already autonomous;
- otherwise ask once, naming the consequence: in `autonomous` there are no intermediate approvals of the design, plan, or result, only the final report; in `interactive` every current approval stays.

The mode holds for the whole run and is never asked again.

Return `action_type`, `operating_mode`, and `workspace_path`. For edit also return `workflow_identity` and `offline_mode`; return `local_source_hint` only when one is already known. For create no edit-source fields are required.
nodes.completionCondition: Action, edit identity, source-access boundary, canonical workspace path, and operating mode are resolved

nodes.directive:
Capture the user's observable workflow goal, identity and visibility, success criteria, approvals, external side effects, important failure behavior, and protected constraints. Ask only for a material decision that cannot be discovered; do not ask the user to design Moira internals.

Use the already materialized workspace at `{{workspace_path}}`. Verify that `process-id.txt` and `workflow-authoring-reference.md` exist; do not rewrite either file. Write the complete requirements once to `workflow-requirements.md`, separating requirements from implementation ideas. Consumers read the canonical file rather than a duplicated context summary.
nodes.completionCondition: The materialized create workspace and authoring reference are verified and the complete canonical requirements file exists

nodes.directive:
Use `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-requirements.md` and the applicable sections of `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-authoring-reference.md` to produce the complete create-side pre-mutation design contract. The path is canonical; reread unchanged content only when it is absent, uncertain, compacted, changed, or exact text is needed.

Inspect actual Moira and project sources. Perform external research only when a material correctness or compatibility question cannot be resolved locally, and record conclusions and sources in the design. Cover the whole requested outcome, responsibilities, branches, dependencies, writer/reader contracts, authority boundaries, failure and recovery behavior, review/repair/replan ownership, and which earlier conclusions become stale after each kind of mutation.

Design acceptance evidence before implementation. For every proposed validation or proof mechanism, name the required state and a plausible wrong state, then name the observation that reliably differs. If no such observation exists, do not specify imitation proof: assign the property to behavioral, architectural, independent, or user judgment, or correct the criterion. Mechanical registry/schema/ID completeness, semantic scenario completeness, and business-meaning provenance are different evidence classes; observing an operation alone proves neither of the latter two.

Prefer existing Moira primitives and bounded composition. Class-wide treatment means all real manifestations of a confirmed defect in the agreed scope, not a universal mechanism for a contextual property. Validation infrastructure is legitimate when it is itself a requested result with a consumer and discriminating outcome; otherwise keep it subordinate to the requested artifact.

Write the complete current design to `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-design.md`. Do not return the graph, node count, research summary, or file contents through workflow context.


When the authored workflow has meaningful user-visible stages, design an optional static execution-progress presentation using the current Moira product schema and documentation. Specify 3–10 ordered milestones, a template-enabled title and labels, bounded readable topology, visible current emphasis, display-only forward/backward connections, complete `progressNodeId` mapping for every observable waiting node, and deterministic many-to-one focus. Explain mobile horizontal readability and whether mapped Telegram attention is authorized. Distinguish the shared JSON projection/visual model used by the always-visible UI and PNG renderer, agent-facing short-lived one-time PNG download metadata, and internal direct `attachProgressImage` Telegram rendering. Omit progress when it would be decorative.

Progress never owns conditions, expressions, routes, status/history/cursor/counters, proof tokens, validation protocols, or another state/layout algorithm. Structural ID/mapping completeness, semantic scenario completeness, and business-meaning provenance require different evidence.

When one mapped milestone represents multiple current roles or needs truthful current unit/iteration detail, consider optional `progressActiveLabel` on the relevant user-visible waiting primary nodes. It is template-enabled and replaces only that exact node's active milestone label; inactive milestones keep the stable base label. Require every referenced variable to be authoritative on every route that can make that node current. Prefer bounded role/counter text and base-label fallback. Never use the field on an unmapped/transient node or to create progress state, conditions, routes, counters, history, proof, or a substitute for a better primary responsibility model.
nodes.completionCondition: The complete current pre-mutation design contract and its evidence model are recorded in the canonical create design file

nodes.directive:
Read the current `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-design.md`, present its structure and observable consequences to the user, and ask whether it is approved.

Return `structure_approved` as `yes` or `no`. When it is `no`, return the user's exact non-empty `structure_feedback`. Do not revise the design here.
nodes.completionCondition: The user approved the current design or supplied actionable rejection feedback

nodes.directive: Apply {{approve-structure.structure_feedback}} to the current `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-design.md` while preserving unaffected requirements in `workflow-requirements.md` and required semantic guarantees. Update the same design file. Use the authoring reference when needed; do not copy the graph into workflow context or force a full reread of unchanged reference content.
nodes.completionCondition: The current workflow design file incorporates the user's feedback

nodes.directive:
Create the actual workflow from the independently reviewed and, in interactive mode, user-approved `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-requirements.md` and `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-design.md`, applying the relevant sections of `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-authoring-reference.md` and using the official Moira workflow CLI and current node/schema contracts.

Own completeness before handoff: implement the whole design, follow its dependencies, preserve every confirmed route and authority boundary, inspect all real manifestations of each confirmed defect class in the agreed scope, and check whole-artifact coherence. Select evidence whose observation distinguishes the required state from a plausible wrong state and whose modality matches the property. Do not create proof machinery merely to demonstrate that another check ran; do not add helper scripts, manifests, handoff protocols, decorative state, universal contextual detectors, or validator state machines without a requested result, a real consumer, and a discriminating effect.

Save the complete workflow at `{{workspace_path}}/workflow.json`. Validate that actual artifact with the official CLI and repair concrete structural errors before completing. After validation, overwrite `{{workspace_path}}/workspace/workflow-schema.txt` using the official `moira-workflow {{workspace_path}}/workflow.json schema` command. Inspect the complete projection for the designed nodes, connections, conditions, starts, teleports, terminals, cycles, reachability classes, dangling targets, data declarations/uses, and complete coverage; confirm semantic meaning in JSON. The projection is derived structural evidence, not semantic proof or a second validator. Return only its path as `workflow_artifact_path`; independent review verifies the completed artifact rather than co-authoring ordinary missing work.


Implement every accepted progress outcome with the current product schema/docs and official CLI. Preserve primary execution routing; array order alone determines completed/current/pending and progress connections only draw. Include template title/labels, bounded readable milestones, visible current role, every real waiting-node mapping, many-to-one focus, and shared projection/model parity across UI and PNG. `attachProgressImage` is allowed only on a mapped Telegram node under existing notification authority and uses direct renderer/photo delivery; do not place an agent one-time download token into workflow state. Reject progress conditions, expressions, status/history/cursor/counters, routes, proof machinery, or duplicate state/layout logic. Validate/project complete structure, then use behavioral and independent judgment for semantic usefulness.

Implement every accepted `progressActiveLabel` through the current schema/docs and official CLI on a mapped user-visible waiting node only. Preserve its base milestone label for inactive states and primary routing/state/focus unchanged. Validate template references and inspect representative initial, active, next-iteration and replan contexts so default or prior values cannot appear as current truth. Keep UI and PNG on the shared projection/model; do not duplicate active-label logic in a consumer.
nodes.completionCondition: The approved workflow exists at the canonical path, passes official structural validation, and has a complete current structural projection generated and inspected before independent review

nodes.directive:
Present the actual resulting workflow at {{workflow_artifact_path}}, its resulting structure, semantic-guarantee outcome, and how it satisfies the user's requirements. Use the approved design or edit plan as applicable. Read the accepted JSON and complete current structural projection at `{{workspace_path}}/workspace/workflow-schema.txt`; describe the actual starts, terminals, affected routes, cycles, reachability, coverage, and data-flow consequences after any repair. State that artifact production required official validation, but do not invent a reader-visible validation report or treat the projection as semantic proof.

nodes.completionCondition: The user received a presentation grounded in the accepted JSON and current complete structural projection and either approved the resulting workflow or supplied actionable final feedback

nodes.directive:
Upload the actual approved workflow at {{workflow_artifact_path}} to the active Moira server. This side effect runs only after user authorization.

Obtain a one-time upload token and POST the file. On the initial request use {{ask-upload.upload_method}}: no special flag for `standard`, `forceNew=true` for `copy_new`, or `adminOverride=true` for `admin_override`. After a genuine upload error, follow the recovery choice you just obtained: `copy_new` and `admin_override` select their named semantics, while `retry` repeats the last user-authorized request method without silently dropping its flags. The recovery choice is already in the current conversation; do not add a persistent method/retry flag or hardcode another server.

Return `upload_success`; on failure also return the concrete `upload_error` consumed by error recovery.
nodes.completionCondition: The authorized upload completed or a concrete error is available to recovery

nodes.directive:
Error occurred while uploading workflow.

Error: {{save-workflow-to-target.upload_error}}

**Analyze the error and offer appropriate options:**

If error contains "owned by another user" or "Access denied":
- This means the workflow ID in JSON file belongs to another user
- Offer options: **copy_new** (create copy with new ID) or **admin_override** (admin only - overwrite original)

For other errors:
- Offer standard options: **retry**, **skip**, **cancel**

Options explanation:
1. **copy_new** - Create a new workflow with fresh ID (ignores ID from JSON, your copy)
2. **admin_override** - Overwrite the original workflow (requires admin privileges)
3. **retry** - Try upload again
4. **skip** - Skip upload, keep workflow saved locally only
5. **cancel** - Cancel everything

Present only relevant options based on error type.
nodes.completionCondition: User selected action

nodes.directive:
Synchronize the approved workflow at {{workflow_artifact_path}} to the existing repository target {{local_workflow_path}} using the official Moira workflow CLI while preserving the target identity. Verify that the resulting local artifact exists and contains the approved workflow. This node is reached only when a real local target exists.

Writing that single resolved target is the requested work of this run and needs no separate approval in either operating mode. Write nothing else: no other repository path, no deletion or rename, and no version-control operation such as commit, push, branch, or stash.
nodes.completionCondition: The approved workflow is synchronized to the real existing local target with identity preserved

nodes.directive:
Analyse the requested change and derive the pre-mutation edit design contract from it, writing both into one document at `{{workspace_path}}/edit-plan.md`: the analysis section first, because the contract is derived from it, then the contract itself. They share one document because they describe one subject; kept apart, a correction made in one of them leaves the other stating the superseded version, and nothing detects the divergence.

Work from `{{workspace_path}}/edit-requirements.md`, the complete workflow at {{workflow_artifact_path}}, the source decision already recorded in `source-provenance.md`, any approved audit scope in {{additional_edit_scope}}, and applicable sections of `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-authoring-reference.md`; that path is canonical and unchanged content need not be reread when already present and certain. Read the current complete structural projection at `{{workspace_path}}/workspace/workflow-schema.txt` with the JSON and trace each affected route and declaration through the complete graph; confirm its semantics in the JSON. A structural projection is navigation and completeness evidence, and neither it nor validator success is semantic proof.

In the analysis, identify affected responsibilities, connections, variables, schemas, artifacts, authority boundaries, and observable routes. Follow dependencies through the complete projected graph to unchanged contract boundaries without turning known entry points into an implementation whitelist. Freeze required semantic guarantees, carry the recorded source decision rather than deriving it again, and record inexpensive baseline diagnostics for turns, reference load, state utilization, counters/protocols, validation amplification, responsibility coherence, and agent freedom. Compare alternatives only for a real trade-off.

In the contract, state for each behavioral outcome the affected contract or area, mandatory invariants, known dependencies, authority and failure boundaries, repair/replan ownership, observable acceptance criteria, evidence modality, and behavioral verification. Before requiring any validation or proof mechanism, name the required and plausible wrong states and the observation that distinguishes them; revise an unprovable criterion instead of specifying surrogate proof. Bound class-wide work to real manifestations of a confirmed cause in the agreed scope.

Preserve the executor's freedom over exploration, decomposition, edit order, and repair tactics. Confirmed nodes are entry points, not an exhaustive whitelist.

The acceptance criteria you write become this run's contract: once the contract has passed independent review, they are not reworded by whoever works to them. Write each one so that it can be observably met or missed, rather than so that it can later be relaxed.

Do not copy the document into workflow context.


When the authored workflow has meaningful user-visible stages, design an optional static execution-progress presentation using the current Moira product schema and documentation. Specify 3–10 ordered milestones, a template-enabled title and labels, bounded readable topology, visible current emphasis, display-only forward/backward connections, complete `progressNodeId` mapping for every observable waiting node, and deterministic many-to-one focus. Explain mobile horizontal readability and whether mapped Telegram attention is authorized. Distinguish the shared JSON projection/visual model used by the always-visible UI and PNG renderer, agent-facing short-lived one-time PNG download metadata, and internal direct `attachProgressImage` Telegram rendering. Omit progress when it would be decorative.

Progress never owns conditions, expressions, routes, status/history/cursor/counters, proof tokens, validation protocols, or another state/layout algorithm. Structural ID/mapping completeness, semantic scenario completeness, and business-meaning provenance require different evidence.

When one mapped milestone represents multiple current roles or needs truthful current unit/iteration detail, consider optional `progressActiveLabel` on the relevant user-visible waiting primary nodes. It is template-enabled and replaces only that exact node's active milestone label; inactive milestones keep the stable base label. Require every referenced variable to be authoritative on every route that can make that node current. Prefer bounded role/counter text and base-label fallback. Never use the field on an unmapped/transient node or to create progress state, conditions, routes, counters, history, proof, or a substitute for a better primary responsibility model.
nodes.completionCondition: One document holds the complete analysis — scope, dependencies, frozen guarantees, source decision, and baseline diagnostics — followed by the outcome-oriented edit design contract and its evidence model, and both account for all affected routes and declarations in the current complete structural projection

nodes.directive:
Read `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-design-review.md`, reproduce every reported edit-plan-owned defect against the current `edit-plan.md` with its analysis, the requirements, the original workflow, and `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-authoring-reference.md`, and classify the earliest cause before changing anything. Repair all real manifestations of a confirmed plan-owned cause in the agreed scope, not only the cited sentence, while preserving implementation freedom.

Return `changed` only after updating the same plan with a coherent correction; include a concise `root_cause_class` and `changed_knowledge` that name the relevant design knowledge changed for the next reviewer. Reject false, duplicate, stylistic, delivery-only, and speculative findings. Return `reassess` without mutation when reproduction shows that the requirements, a criterion, or the evidence model is invalid or unprovable; do not disguise that as plan repair or add surrogate validation machinery. Do not copy findings or the corrected plan into workflow context.
nodes.completionCondition: The finding is classified and either a real plan repair with consumed changed-knowledge evidence exists or reassessment is explicitly selected

nodes.directive:
Read `{{workspace_path}}/edit-plan.md`, present its current structure, behavioral changes, protected guarantees, and resulting graph to the user, and ask whether it is approved.

Return `plan_approval` as `yes` or `no`. When it is `no`, return the user's exact non-empty `user_feedback`. Do not revise the plan here.
nodes.completionCondition: The user approved the current plan or supplied actionable rejection feedback

nodes.directive: Apply {{present-edit-plan.user_feedback}} to the same `{{workspace_path}}/edit-plan.md` while preserving unaffected requirements, the verified analysis section of that same document, and semantic guarantees. Change the plan and necessary design dependencies only; do not copy it into workflow context. The revised plan returns to the same independent reviewer.
nodes.completionCondition: The same plan file incorporates the user's feedback and is ready for independent rereview

nodes.directive:
Determine whether the user authorizes uploading the approved workflow. Respect an explicit decision and method already present; otherwise ask in `interactive` mode.

In `autonomous` mode do not ask. When the task carries no explicit upload authorization, return `upload_confirmed: false`. Never select `copy_new` or `admin_override` on your own: a non-standard method requires the user's explicit authorization of its observable semantics.

If approved, return `upload_confirmed: true` and the request method: `standard`, `copy_new`, or `admin_override`. Do not perform the upload here.
nodes.completionCondition: The upload decision and any authorized request method are resolved without asking in autonomous mode

nodes.directive:
Independently review the complete structurally valid workflow at {{workflow_artifact_path}} against the applicable requirements, the independently reviewed design for a created workflow or the edit plan with its analysis for an edited one, the complete current structural projection at `{{workspace_path}}/workspace/workflow-schema.txt`, and `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-authoring-reference.md`. Read primary sources directly. Review the agreed result as a whole while staying within the user's original scope and authority; do not run linters or repeat structural validation here.

Use the projection to trace every affected success, refusal, repair, replan, recovery, cancellation, terminal, and teleport route, including conditions, cycles, reachability classes, dangling targets, coverage, and data declarations/uses; verify their semantics and authority in the complete JSON. The projection supplies complete structural facts but cannot prove semantic correctness, requirement coverage, or that another role performed a check.

Report every current reproducible blocking defect in `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-quality-review.md` and classify its earliest cause: workflow-artifact defect, validation/test defect, insufficient existing evidence, documentation/projection defect, invalid or unprovable criterion, or upstream plan/process defect. A documentation or projection issue is artifact-owned only when that document or projection is itself part of the requested result. Classify each frozen guarantee as `IMPROVED`, `PRESERVED`, `REGRESSED`, or `UNVERIFIED`.

For every claimed proof mechanism, require the required state, a plausible wrong state, and an observation that reliably differs. A surrogate signal is not semantic or business-provenance evidence when the same observation can arise in the wrong state. {{#if fix-quality-issues.root_cause_class}}The immediately preceding repair reported root `{{fix-quality-issues.root_cause_class}}` and changed knowledge/reach `{{fix-quality-issues.changed_knowledge}}`; compare these claims with the actual artifact and current findings. If the same root finding returns without stronger discriminating evidence or a changed relevant source of truth, return `replan` rather than requesting another layer of the same mechanism.{{/if}} Also return `replan` when recent cycles change only validation/reporting infrastructure while the requested result and its direct evidence do not improve.

Return one aggregate `quality_review_outcome`: `pass` when there are no blockers; `repair` only when every blocker is a confirmed defect owned by the workflow artifact within the approved result; `replan` when any blocker belongs to validation, evidence, documentation outside the requested artifact, a criterion, requirements interpretation, plan, or process. Mixed causes return `replan`. Zero findings is normal. Do not repair, expand scope, design machinery, or require a universal detector for a contextual property.


When progress is applicable, independently inspect the current design/artifact for template title and labels, 3–10 bounded readable milestones, visible current emphasis, horizontal/mobile behavior, complete observable-wait mapping, deterministic focus, and coherent forward/backward display edges. Verify the shared JSON projection/model remains the single UI/PNG source, agent one-time download metadata is not confused with internal direct Telegram rendering, and every `attachProgressImage` node is mapped and authorized. Block dynamic/state/routing progress fields, consumer drift, incomplete mappings, misleading milestone semantics, and evidence that treats a call/counter/token as proof of semantic completeness or business provenance. Official validation/schema proves structural facts only; scenario behavior and independent judgment own meaning/readability.

When active-only detail is applicable, independently verify that `progressActiveLabel` is on a mapped user-visible waiting node, remains bounded/readable, falls back to the stable base label when inactive, and references only variables authoritative on every route reaching that node. Block undefined/stale counters, misleading role detail, inactive-label drift, wrong/unmapped scope, consumer-specific override logic, routing/state semantics, and treating a rendered counter as proof of business completeness.
nodes.completionCondition: The current independent semantic review is recorded once after direct inspection of the complete JSON and current structural projection, and its pass, repair, or replan outcome matches the classified blocking causes

nodes.directive:
Read `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-quality-review.md`, reproduce every blocking finding against the actual workflow, its complete current structural projection at `{{workspace_path}}/workspace/workflow-schema.txt`, requirements, the reviewed design or the edit plan with its analysis, and `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-authoring-reference.md`, and classify the earliest cause before changing anything.

Return `changed` only when every finding is a confirmed workflow-artifact defect within the approved result. Repair all real manifestations of the confirmed root in the agreed scope, not merely the cited location, but do not turn a contextual property into a universal detector. Use the official Moira workflow CLI and validate the changed artifact. For every changed artifact, overwrite `{{workspace_path}}/workspace/workflow-schema.txt` with the official `moira-workflow {{workflow_artifact_path}} schema` command and inspect the refreshed complete projection for the repaired routes, declarations, reachability, cycles, dangling targets, and coverage before returning. Return a concise `root_cause_class` plus `changed_knowledge` describing the actual changed source/reach and why the next review now has a stronger or different observation. Changed bytes or additional surrogate machinery without changed relevant knowledge is not a repair.

Return `reassess` without mutating the artifact or fabricating refreshed evidence when the finding is not reproducible, the criterion or evidence model is invalid, the proposed observation cannot distinguish the required state from a plausible wrong state, the same root returned without stronger evidence, or the work has drifted into validation-only infrastructure. Do not weaken the user's goal or start an unchanged review loop.
nodes.completionCondition: The finding is classified and either a real validated artifact repair with a refreshed complete structural projection and consumed transition evidence exists, or reassessment is explicitly selected without artifact mutation

nodes.directive:
Decide whether an optional full antipattern audit of the complete original workflow runs before edit planning. Respect an explicit answer already present.

In `autonomous` mode decide it yourself from the requested change and the evidence you already have: choose `yes` when the source is unknown, large, or suspected of carrying defects beyond the requested cone, and `no` when the change is narrow and the source was recently audited. Do not ask the user.

In `interactive` mode ask, explaining that `yes` audits the whole source and lets the user select confirmed repairs, while `no` limits analysis to the requested cone and necessary dependencies.

Return only `full_antipattern_audit` as `yes` or `no`. Do not perform the audit or reset any previously approved scope here.
nodes.completionCondition: The audit scope decision is resolved by the user in interactive mode or by the agent in autonomous mode

nodes.directive:
Audit the complete original workflow at {{workflow_artifact_path}} against `{{workspace_path}}/workflow-authoring-reference.md`. Read both primary sources directly, and read the complete current structural projection at `{{workspace_path}}/workspace/workflow-schema.txt`. Use the projection to inspect the whole node/edge corpus, starts, teleports, terminals, reachability classes, cycles, dangling targets, schema coverage, and declared data flow; confirm conditions, directives, schemas, variables, writers/readers, reachable routes, artifacts, and engine semantics against the complete JSON. Structural output is evidence, not semantic proof. Include pre-existing findings; exclude style and speculative robustness.

Overwrite `{{workspace_path}}/full-antipattern-audit.md` with the complete current report, showing every confirmed finding with its evidence.

In `interactive` mode ask which repairs join this edit. In `autonomous` mode select the scope yourself, without asking: include the confirmed findings that block the requested outcome or that are safe and directly adjacent to it, and leave the rest recorded in the report for a later run.

Return only the concise resulting `additional_edit_scope`, or `none`; do not copy the report into context or repair here.
nodes.completionCondition: The complete original workflow and its current complete structural projection are audited directly against the authoring reference, the current report is on disk, and additional repair scope is selected under the existing mode contract

nodes.directive:
Prepare the complete edit source in the already materialized correlated workspace at `{{workspace_path}}`.

Use the edit identity in {{get-action-type.workflow_identity}} and offline mode {{get-action-type.offline_mode}}. {{#if get-action-type.local_source_hint}}Use this explicit local source hint: {{get-action-type.local_source_hint}}.{{/if}} Do not ask for facts already present. Verify that `process-id.txt` and `workflow-authoring-reference.md` already exist; do not rewrite either file.

Resolve explicit paths, public owner/slug, internal UUID, and bundled metadata as possible identities of the same workflow. In offline mode use only local sources. Otherwise obtain the complete server definition through a one-time download token and locate any repository definition. Preserve complete candidates and record provenance and semantic differences in `source-provenance.md`. Use the sole unambiguous source automatically. If materially different valid sources remain, decide by mode. In `interactive` mode show their semantic differences and ask the user to select local, server, or a designed reconciliation. In `autonomous` mode decide on evidence — provenance, version order, and which definition the requested change actually targets — record the decision and its justification in `source-provenance.md`, and ask only when the evidence genuinely cannot decide.
